name: Echoes of the Force
throughline_question: Can someone who survived by hiding ever find the courage to stand in the open again?

allegiances.description: Survivors of Order 66 who have hidden their connection to the Force, living in exile while the Empire hunts them. Now the Force is calling them back.

character_variants.pitch: A Togruta healer hiding in the Outer Rim, haunted by visions of a place she has never been — a hidden temple calling her through the Force. The Empire's Inquisitors are hunting survivors. The Force is done waiting.
character_variants.starting_situation: Talia has been living as a frontier healer on the remote world of Lothal's outer settlements. The visions started three weeks ago — a temple buried beneath stone, a voice calling her name, a darkness closing in. This morning, an Imperial shuttle landed at the settlement. They are asking about Force-sensitives.
character_variants.voice_baseline: Quiet, measured. Speaks with the precision of someone who learned that words have weight. Listens more than she talks. Carries grief without drowning in it.
character_variants.background: A Togruta survivor of Order 66 who was a Jedi youngling when the Temple fell. Smuggled offworld by a sympathetic clone trooper, she spent fifteen years hiding her connection to the Force in the Outer Rim.

integration_layer.entry_point: Talia must flee her settlement as the Empire closes in, following Force visions toward a hidden Jedi temple.
integration_layer.personal_stakes: If the Inquisitors find her, she dies. If she ignores the visions, the knowledge in the temple is lost forever. If she uses the dark side to survive, she becomes what she fears.

anchor_adaptations.the_call: Talia's visions intensify as the Empire arrives at her settlement, forcing her to flee
anchor_adaptations.the_companion: Talia encounters another Force survivor and must decide whether to trust them
anchor_adaptations.the_temple: Talia reaches the hidden temple and confronts the trials within
anchor_adaptations.the_choice: Talia faces the Inquisitor and must choose who she truly is

weapons.narrative_note: Built during her years at the Temple, the crystal sings faintly when danger is near.

special_items.mechanical_effect: Once per session, can meditate to add 1 boost die to a Lore or Discipline check related to Jedi knowledge.
special_items.narrative_note: A shard of crystal that once held the teachings of a Jedi archivist.

special_items.name: Clone trooper dog tag
special_items.mechanical_effect: No mechanical effect. Narrative significance only.
special_items.narrative_note: CT-7729. The trooper who carried her out of the Temple.

allegiances.description: Force-sensitive beings who never received Jedi training but feel the pull of something greater. Self-taught, unorthodox, dangerous in their ignorance.

character_variants.pitch: A Zabrak drifter who discovered he could move things with his mind during a bar fight on Tatooine. No training. No philosophy. Just raw power and the growing certainty that something in the galaxy wants him to find it.
character_variants.starting_situation: Kael has been drifting from system to system, drawn by instinct toward something he cannot name. The visions started after a near-death experience in the Kessel mines. Now something is pulling him toward the Outer Rim — and something else is following.
character_variants.voice_baseline: Blunt, restless. Speaks in short sentences. Trusts actions over words. Uncomfortable with stillness. Humor is rare but genuine when it surfaces.
character_variants.background: A Zabrak from Iridonia who left home young and survived on instinct, odd jobs, and a talent for violence. The Force awoke in him during a cave-in — he held up a collapsing wall long enough for three miners to escape. He cannot explain how.

integration_layer.entry_point: Kael arrives on the same world drawn by visions he doesn't understand, colliding with events already in motion.
integration_layer.personal_stakes: Kael has no framework for what he is. Without guidance, his power could consume him. The dark side feels natural — that terrifies him more than anything.

anchor_adaptations.the_call: Kael's visions drive him to the same region, where Imperial activity forces him into hiding
anchor_adaptations.the_companion: Kael encounters someone who can explain what he is — and must decide whether to learn
anchor_adaptations.the_temple: Kael faces trials designed for trained Jedi with nothing but raw power and instinct
anchor_adaptations.the_choice: Kael must choose between the easy power of the dark side and the harder path of discipline

weapons.name: Vibrosword
weapons.narrative_note: Won in a fight he does not talk about. The blade hums at a frequency that makes teeth ache.

armor.name: Battered durasteel cuirass
armor.narrative_note: Salvaged from a decommissioned clone trooper set. Scratched, dented, functional.

tools.name: Survival pack
tools.mechanical_effect: Removes 1 setback from Survival checks in wilderness environments.
tools.narrative_note: Everything a drifter needs. Nothing a drifter doesn't.

special_items.name: Kyber crystal shard (uncut)
special_items.mechanical_effect: Can be used to construct a lightsaber during the campaign if the character gains the knowledge.
special_items.narrative_note: Found in the rubble of the mine collapse. It vibrated in his hand and has not stopped since.

acts.name: The Call
acts.opening_situation: Talia has been living quietly in a frontier settlement on Lothal's outer plains for two years. This morning, the visions intensified — a temple buried beneath volcanic stone on a world she has never visited, a voice she almost recognizes calling her name, and a spreading darkness that tastes like ash. An Imperial shuttle has landed at the settlement. Two figures in dark armor are questioning the locals about anyone with unusual abilities. The Force is screaming at her to run.
acts.opening_location: Lothal, outer settlement — a cluster of moisture farms and repair shops on the edge of the grass plains
acts.galactic_context: The Empire's Inquisitorius program has entered its second decade. Most surviving Jedi have been found and eliminated. The remaining few are the ones who hid deepest. But the Emperor's servants are patient, and their methods are improving. Rumors of a 'Project Harvester' — a systematic Force-sensitive detection program — have reached even the Outer Rim.
open_threads: What is the temple in the visions?
Who is the voice calling through the Force?
Why are the Inquisitors here now — coincidence or something else?
Can Talia flee without endangering the settlement?

xp_bonus_conditions.description: Player engages meaningfully with the Force visions and the decision to flee
Player uses 3+ different skills during the act
Player faces a moral choice involving the dark side or protecting others at personal cost

acts.name: The Companion
acts.opening_situation: Talia has escaped the settlement and followed the Force visions across Lothal to the ruins of an old Jedi waystation. Inside, she finds signs of recent habitation — and a trail leading into the wilderness. She is not the only one the Force has called. Behind her, the Inquisitor's trail grows cold but does not end.
acts.opening_location: Lothal, abandoned Jedi waystation in the northern grasslands
acts.galactic_context: The Grand Inquisitor has dispatched a Second Brother to Lothal following anomalous Force readings in the region. Imperial garrison forces are conducting sweeps of the outer settlements. The Rebel cell on Lothal is keeping its head down, unwilling to draw attention. For now, Talia is on her own.

xp_bonus_conditions.description: Player engages meaningfully with the other Force survivor
Player uses a Force power in a meaningful situation
Player meaningfully engages with consequences of a failed check

acts.name: The Temple
acts.opening_situation: The visions have led Talia to a remote volcanic island on an ocean world called Eshara, far from Imperial lanes. The temple is real — a structure of black stone half-swallowed by lava flows, older than the Republic. Inside, the Force is dense, heavy, and alive. This place was designed to test those who enter it. It has been waiting.
acts.opening_location: Eshara, volcanic island — exterior of the buried Jedi temple
acts.galactic_context: The Second Brother has tracked the Force trail offworld. An Imperial light cruiser has entered the Eshara system. The clock is ticking — the temple's trials must be completed before the Inquisitor arrives.

time_skip.framing: One month of travel. Talia and her companion have moved through the Outer Rim by freighter, fuel transport, and once — memorably — by hitching a ride on a Jawa sandcrawler on Tatooine. The Force visions have sharpened into coordinates. Eshara. A world that does not appear on Imperial star charts.

vignettes.passage:
The cargo hold of the freighter Dustwalker is cramped and smells of engine grease. It is 0300 hours by the ship's chrono, and Talia cannot sleep. The visions press against her consciousness like water against a dam.

She sits cross-legged on the cold floor and reaches for the calm she was taught as a youngling. Breathe. Release. Let the Force flow through, not into. The technique is fifteen years rusty, but the Force does not care about rust. It cares about willingness.

The lightsaber sits in her lap. She has not ignited it in years. The weight of it is both familiar and alien — like a word on the tip of her tongue in a language she used to speak fluently.

choices.text: Ignite the blade. Slowly. Feel the crystal's song and remember what it meant to be a Jedi.
choices.narrative_consequence: The blue light fills the cargo hold. It is smaller than she remembers, more intimate. The hum vibrates in her montrals — a frequency that maps to safety, to belonging, to a life that ended but did not die. Her hands remember the first position. Her body remembers the second. By the time she extinguishes the blade, tears are running down her face, but she is smiling.

choices.text: Meditate without the lightsaber. The Force is more than a weapon. Remember that first.
choices.narrative_consequence: The Force opens like a door she forgot she had the key to. For twenty minutes she floats in it — not the visions, not the urgency, but the thing beneath. The living current that connects everything. She feels the crew sleeping above. She feels the stars turning. She feels, distantly, the temple waiting. When she surfaces, she is calmer than she has been in months.

choices.text: Push deeper into the visions. Force them open. You need answers, not peace.
choices.narrative_consequence: The vision cracks open like an egg. She sees the temple — corridors of black stone, a chamber at the heart, something sealed inside that pulses with light. But she pushes too hard. The vision twists. She sees the Inquisitor's red blade. She sees herself, but wrong — eyes yellow, mouth set in a line of cold purpose. She gasps back to consciousness with a nosebleed and the taste of copper. The Force gave her what she asked for. It always does.

vignettes.passage:
On Tatooine, between transports, Talia sees a child with a broken arm in the Mos Eisley market. The mother is frantic, the local medic is drunk, and the bone is set wrong. It will heal crooked without intervention.

Talia's hands know what to do. The medical kit is in her bag. But healing with the Force — really healing, the way Master Che taught the younglings — would be faster, cleaner, and would leave no trace of the break. It would also be a beacon to anyone looking for Force-sensitives in the area.

choices.text: Use the medical kit. Hands and tools, no Force. It is the safe choice, and it will still help.
choices.narrative_consequence: She sets the bone properly, splints it, and gives the mother instructions in a calm voice that hides the ache in her chest. The child stops crying. The mother offers credits that Talia refuses. It is good work. Honest work. But she knows the Force could have done it better, and the knowledge sits like a stone.

choices.text: Use the Force, subtly. Accelerate the healing through touch. The risk is small, and the child's pain is real.
choices.narrative_consequence: She holds the child's arm and lets the Force flow — not a wave but a trickle, gentle, guided. The bone knits. The swelling fades. The child stares at her with wide eyes. The mother whispers something that might be 'Jedi' and might be 'angel.' Talia leaves quickly. In the alley behind the market, her hands shake. Not from effort — from how natural it felt.

choices.text: Walk away. You cannot help everyone, and every act of compassion here is a risk to your mission.
choices.narrative_consequence: She walks past. The child's crying follows her for three blocks. She tells herself it is necessary — that the temple matters more, that the greater good demands sacrifice. The words are true. They taste like ash. That night, she dreams of the Temple crèche and the younglings she used to play with, and wakes with her jaw clenched so tight her teeth ache.

vignettes.passage:
The vision comes in hyperspace, between Tatooine and Eshara. It is different from the others.

She sees the Temple — but not the Jedi Temple. The Sith temple beneath it, the one they whispered about in the archives but never visited. She sees a figure kneeling before an altar of red crystal, and the figure is wearing her face. The dark-side version of herself speaks, and the words are perfectly clear: 'The light could not save them. You know this.'

The vision does not end. It waits.

choices.text: Reject it. Release the vision into the Force and return to the present. The dark side shows you what it wants you to see, not what is true.
choices.narrative_consequence: She breathes out. Lets go. The vision dissolves like smoke, and she is back in the freighter's crew compartment with the hum of the hyperdrive and the smell of recycled air. Her hands are steady. The dark side's argument is seductive because it is partly true — the light did not save the Jedi Order. But survival is not the same as wisdom, and Talia knows the difference.

choices.text: Listen. Not agree — just listen. The dark side has information, even if its conclusions are wrong.
choices.narrative_consequence: The dark version of herself tilts her head and smiles. 'You are more honest than the others.' It shows her something — a room in the temple, a test that cannot be passed by light alone. Then the vision ends on its own terms. Talia files the information away and does not think about the fact that the dark side smiled at her like a friend.

choices.text: Engage it. Answer back. 'The light saved me. That is enough.'
choices.narrative_consequence: The dark version laughs — not cruelly, almost fondly. 'We will see.' The vision shatters, and Talia feels something shift in the Force. Not a battle won, but a line drawn. The temple ahead feels clearer now, as though her declaration has tuned her to its frequency.

acts.name: The Choice
acts.opening_situation: The temple's trials are behind her. What Talia found at the heart of the temple is a choice — not an artifact or a weapon but a nexus in the Force, a place where the boundary between light and dark is thin enough to reach through. The knowledge of the old Jedi is here, preserved in crystal. So is a Sith holocron, hidden beneath the altar, pulsing with power. And outside, the Inquisitor has arrived. The decision cannot be postponed.
acts.opening_location: Heart of the Eshara temple — the Nexus Chamber
acts.galactic_context: The Second Brother has brought a full Imperial task force to Eshara. TIE fighters patrol the skies. Stormtroopers are establishing a perimeter around the volcanic island. There is no easy escape. Whatever happens in this temple will define who Talia becomes.

npc_roster.name: Serath Vos
npc_roster.role: Imperial Inquisitor (Second Brother) — the primary antagonist hunting Force-sensitive survivors
npc_roster.motivation: Obedience to the Empire and the dark side — but beneath the mask, doubt. Serath was once a Jedi Padawan who broke under torture. He hunts survivors because the alternative is admitting what he became.
npc_roster.voice_notes: Cold, precise, controlled. Speaks like a blade — economy of words, every one placed to cut. But occasionally, in unguarded moments, something older surfaces. A hesitation. A flash of the Padawan he was. These moments pass quickly and are followed by increased aggression.
behavioral_envelope: Fights with controlled aggression — Makashi-influenced form, elegant and lethal
Will attempt to turn the player character rather than simply kill them in early encounters
Shows cracks in composure when confronted with genuine compassion or Jedi teachings
If disposition rises above 0.5, begins questioning his path openly

Absent but closing — tracking the hyperspace trail to Eshara. His arrival is the ticking clock of Act 3.
Final confrontation — arrives at the temple. This is the climax. The player must face him, and the outcome depends on their choices throughout the campaign.

npc_roster.name: Mirra Solus
npc_roster.role: Another Force-sensitive survivor — a former Jedi archivist who has been guarding knowledge in exile
npc_roster.motivation: Preserve what the Jedi knew. Mirra believes the Order failed because it forgot its own teachings, and she has spent fifteen years collecting fragments — holocrons, texts, oral traditions — to ensure the knowledge survives.
npc_roster.voice_notes: Warm, scholarly, slightly absent-minded in the way of someone whose thoughts are always half in a library. But beneath the warmth, steel. Mirra has survived this long by being smarter, more careful, and more ruthless about her mission than anyone expects.
behavioral_envelope: Never initiates violence but is capable of defending herself
Offers knowledge freely but tests whether the player is ready for it
Will sacrifice herself for the knowledge she carries — but only as a last resort
Grows more trusting as the player demonstrates light-side choices
Disposition drops sharply if the player uses dark-side powers casually

npc_roster.name: CT-7729 (Ghost)
npc_roster.role: The clone trooper who saved Talia during Order 66 — status unknown, but rumors of a defected clone matching his description have surfaced
npc_roster.motivation: Atonement. Ghost disobeyed the order, but he could not save the others. He has spent fifteen years running from what the clones became, living under aliases in the Outer Rim.
npc_roster.voice_notes: Clipped, military cadence softened by years of civilian life. Calls Talia 'kid' even though she is no longer one. Dry humor. Uncomfortable with gratitude. Still checks exits when entering a room.
